Usage Guide for LLMs and Agents

Source: vignettes/articles/llm-usage.Rmd
llm-usage.Rmd

This page is for language models and coding agents that use griddy on behalf of a user. It states the current API exactly, including the functions added in 0.2.0, which may postdate your training data. A machine-readable index of this site is at llms.txt. Every page also has a Markdown version at the same address, with .md in place of .html.

What this package is

griddy measures how values in a spatial panel move between classes over time. It estimates classic and spatial Markov chains, summarizes them, tests whether transition dynamics differ across regimes, and measures rank mobility. Inputs are long data frames or sf objects. Outputs are tidy tables, S3 objects with print methods, and ggplot2 plots. The methods follow Rey (2001) and Rey, Kang, and Wolf (2016). PySAL giddy is the Python reference implementation; Coverage of PySAL giddy maps each of its features to a griddy function, a short recipe, or another package.

Input shape

One row per unit per period. id, time, and value are bare column names (tidy evaluation), not strings.

For spatial Markov, pass geometry: an sf tibble with one row per unit, taken from a single period, carrying nb and wt list-columns from sfdep. Its rows are matched to units by id: through a column with the same name as id, or through the column named in geometry_id. listw and nb arguments are accepted for older code; prefer geometry.

geom <- geography |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    nb = sfdep::st_contiguity(geometry),
    wt = sfdep::st_weights(nb)
  )

Functions

These are the exported functions in griddy 0.2.0, with their exact signatures.

# Classification and chains
classify_dynamics(data, id, time, value,
  method = c("pooled_quantile", "time_quantile", "fixed", "existing"),
  k = 5, breaks = NULL, labels = NULL)
markov_dynamics(classes, id, time, state = class)
spatial_markov(data, id, time, value,
  geometry = NULL, geometry_id = NULL, listw = NULL, nb = NULL,
  k = 5, lag_k = k,
  class_method = c("pooled_quantile", "time_quantile", "fixed"),
  zero.policy = TRUE)
transition_matrix(x, type = c("probability", "count"), lag_class = NULL)
class_intervals(x, ...)
lag_intervals(x)

# Chain summaries (x is a grd_markov object or a probability matrix)
steady_state(x)
sojourn_time(x)       # new in 0.2.0
first_passage(x)      # new in 0.2.0
mobility_index(x,     # new in 0.2.0
  measure = c("prais", "determinant", "eigen", "bartholomew1", "bartholomew2"),
  initial = NULL)

# Inference (x is a grd_spatial_markov object or a list of count matrices)
homogeneity_test(x, ...)  # new in 0.2.0

# Rank mobility and plots
rank_mobility(data, id, time, value,
  compare = c("endpoint", "adjacent"), descending = TRUE)
plot_transition_matrix(x)
plot_spatial_markov(x)
plot_rank_mobility(x)

What each one returns:

  • classify_dynamics(): the input with an ordered class column, as a grd_classes object.
  • markov_dynamics(): a grd_markov object with transitions (one row per unit and step) and matrix (one row per cell).
  • spatial_markov(): a grd_spatial_markov object. transitions adds lag_class and spatial_lag. matrix is keyed by lag_class, from_state, and to_state.
  • transition_matrix(): a base matrix. With lag_class, the conditional matrix for that spatial-lag class.
  • steady_state(), sojourn_time(): named numeric vectors. first_passage(): a matrix.
  • mobility_index(): a named vector with all five measures by default.
  • homogeneity_test(): a tibble with columns test, statistic, df, and p_value, and rows chi2, likelihood_ratio, and kullback.
  • rank_mobility(): the input with ranks added. Endpoint comparisons add start_time, end_time, start_rank, and end_rank; adjacent comparisons add to_time and to_rank. Both add rank_change and abs_rank_change.

A complete workflow

The bundled usjoin panel has per-capita income for 48 US states from 1929 to 2009.

library(griddy)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(sfdep)

data(usjoin)
data(us_states, package = "spData")

geom <- us_states |>
  filter(NAME %in% usjoin$name) |>
  mutate(nb = st_contiguity(geometry), wt = st_weights(nb))

relative <- usjoin |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(rel_income = income / mean(income)) |>
  ungroup()

chain <- relative |>
  classify_dynamics(name, year, rel_income, k = 5) |>
  markov_dynamics(name, year, class)

sojourn_time(chain)
#>        Q1        Q2        Q3        Q4        Q5 
#> 11.712121  5.765152  4.860759  6.603448 16.083333
mobility_index(chain, "prais")
#>     prais 
#> 0.1695447

spatial <- spatial_markov(
  relative, name, year, rel_income,
  geometry = geom, geometry_id = NAME, k = 5
)
homogeneity_test(spatial)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   test             statistic    df  p_value
#>   <chr>                <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 chi2                  201.    60 4.72e-17
#> 2 likelihood_ratio      171.    60 1.49e-12
#> 3 kullback              171.    60 1.49e-12

Pitfalls

  • Give the weights ids. spatial_markov() matches the rows of geometry to units through a column with the same name as id, or through the column named in geometry_id, so row order does not matter. For listw or nb, it uses the region ids when they are the values of id; set them with spdep::poly2nb(x, row.names = x$id). Without usable ids it matches rows by position, in ascending order of id, and warns. Do not ignore that warning: weights in any other row order give units the wrong neighbors. Before 0.2.0, rows were always matched by position, with no warning.
  • Build nb and wt last. They refer to rows of geometry by position. Filtering or reordering geometry after building them gives units the wrong neighbors, and matching by id cannot detect it.
  • Balance the panel for spatial Markov. Every unit must appear in every period, and the weights must cover exactly the panel’s units; spatial_markov() stops otherwise.
  • Use relative values for chain summaries. With pooled breaks on a growing nominal series, units drift into the top class and stay there. The chain becomes absorbing: steady_state() puts all mass in the top class, sojourn_time() returns Inf, and first_passage() stops with an error. Divide by the period mean or median before classifying, as in the workflow above.
  • first_passage() needs an irreducible chain: every class reachable from every other.
  • Empty rows are NA. A class with no departures has NA probabilities, not zeros, and zero counts. Conditional matrices for spatial-lag classes often have such rows. The coverage article shows how to fill them the way giddy’s fill_empty_classes does.
  • Lag classes are measured at the start of each transition, from the spatial lag in from_time.
  • kullback equals likelihood_ratio. With origin-state margins the two statistics are identical, and both use the Bickenbach and Bode (2003) degrees of freedom. Do not report them as independent evidence.
  • Pass counts, not probabilities, to homogeneity_test(). For regimes other than spatial-lag classes, pass a list of count matrices with the same dimensions.
  • Rank direction. With descending = TRUE (the default), the largest value has rank 1, and a positive rank_change means a unit moved up.

What griddy does not do

  • Full and geographic rank Markov chains, the Kendall’s tau family including LIMA, and rose diagrams are planned. The coverage article has recipes for the rank chains with existing functions.
  • Sequence analysis is out of scope; use TraMineR.
  • Communicating, recurrent, and absorbing class analysis of reducible chains is out of scope; use markovchain.

References

Bickenbach, F., and Bode, E. (2003). Evaluating the Markov property in studies of economic convergence. International Regional Science Review, 26(3), 363–392. https://doi.org/10.1177/0160017603253789

Rey, S. J. (2001). Spatial empirics for economic growth and convergence. Geographical Analysis, 33(3), 195–214. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1538-4632.2001.tb00444.x

Rey, S. J., Kang, W., and Wolf, L. (2016). The properties of tests for spatial effects in discrete Markov chain models of regional income distribution dynamics. Journal of Geographical Systems, 18(4), 377–398. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10109-016-0234-x
